newsitem.title: CANADA: CanWest in deal to boost Network Ten stake.
newsitem.headline: CanWest in deal to boost Network Ten stake.

text.p: CanWest Global Communications Corp said on Thursday it entered into a series of deals with an unrelated Australian company, Donholken Pty Ltd, to enable CanWest to acquire a 20 percent voting and a 10 percent equitable interest in Network Ten.
CanWest said it advanced the purchaser C$150 million through an affiliate.

The deal will increase CanWest's economic interest in Network Ten to 76 percent from 66 percent, although under Australian media foreign ownership laws CanWest is restricted to a 15 percent voting interest.

CanWest initially held a 15-percent voting and 57.5-percent economic interest in Network Ten. In November it entered into similar deals with an Australian investment company who bought 17 percent of the voting shares in the Network and lifted CanWest's economic interest to 66 percent.
The Australian Broadcasting Authority is reviewing the deal to see if it complies with foreign control provisions.

"We are cooperating fully with the ABA, and ... we are quite confident that the appropriateness of these transactions will be found to comply fully with all law and regulations," said CanWest vice-president Tom Strike.
CanWest said the increase in CanWest's holdings may be scaled back if Network Ten can successfully attract a public float of its shares.

"We have always supported the idea of bringing the public into Network Ten, but have resisted having our interests diluted in order to do so," said CanWest chief executive Israel Asper. "Hopefully, these transactions will support both objectives."
The Australian government has launched a media inquiry into ownership rules and is expected to table proposed legislation in the next month or two.
"Clearly, that may have a major bearing on our future investment in Network Ten," said Strike.

Network Ten contributed C$58 million to CanWest's August 31, 1996 year-end after-tax profits. CanWest is forecasting an increase in 1997, which will be augmented by the increased economic interest which will be fully absorbed by CanWest in its second and third quarters of 1997, CanWest said.
